title: The Great Chip Rotation: AMD, Intel, Nvidia Slide as Investors Flee to Big Tech Software

body:
Semiconductor stocks extended their brutal selloff on Friday as investors continued rotating out of AI chip names and into relatively cheaper Big Tech software and internet stocks, marking one of the most significant sector rotations of 2026.

Shares of Nvidia, Intel, Advanced Micro Devices, Qualcomm, Marvell Technology, and SanDisk fell between 3% and 7% in Friday's opening trade. The Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X Shares ETF (SOXL) plunged about 16%, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) dropped nearly 5%. The PHLX Semiconductor Index has now fallen more than 13% since its late June peak.

Strong Earnings, Weak Sentiment

The selloff comes despite fundamentally strong results across the chip sector. TSMC posted record second-quarter revenue of $40.2 billion, a 32.2% year-over-year increase that landed at the top of its own guidance range, with earnings per share surging 52.6%. The company also raised its capital expenditure forecast to $60–64 billion and announced plans to invest an additional $100 billion in its Arizona operations.

Yet TSMC shares fell nearly 2% on the day. JPMorgan's Global Market Strategist Hugh Gimber said the chip sector's next leg higher "depends on continued Big Tech AI spending," noting the selloff is "not a reflection of weakening fundamentals" but rather investors questioning whether rapid earnings growth can continue.

Where the Money Is Going

The rotation is flowing into old Magnificent Seven favorites. Apple has surged 20% from its June low after receiving China approval for Apple Intelligence. Meta Platforms has climbed 25.5%, and Microsoft has gained 12%. Bank of America's fund-manager survey found semiconductors remain the "world's most crowded trade," but crucially, "no one is short" — meaning a further unwind could have room to run.

Two stocks alone — Micron and Nvidia — are expected to contribute a staggering 40% of S&P 500 earnings growth in the second quarter, according to Goldman Sachs, highlighting the concentration risk that makes some investors nervous.

India's Chip Ambitions in Context

For Indian semiconductor professionals, the rotation carries mixed signals. India's ambitious push to build domestic chip fabrication capacity — backed by government incentives and partnerships with companies like Micron, which is building an assembly plant in Gujarat — remains on track regardless of short-term stock volatility. However, the selloff highlights how dependent the global chip ecosystem remains on AI spending from U.S. hyperscalers.

Indian-origin engineers hold senior positions across Nvidia, AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm. The current market turbulence underscores both the opportunity and the risk: India's semiconductor talent pool is world-class, but the industry's fortunes are tightly linked to whether AI capital expenditures justify today's sky-high valuations. All eyes turn to Intel's earnings next Thursday for the next major data point.
author: Diaspora Desk
